hints.title: Hamming Distance Constraint
hints.text: A valid step from index j to index i requires groups[j] does not equal groups[i], len(words[j]) == len(words[i]), and Hamming distance between the words strictly equal to 1.

hints.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence Framework
hints.text: Since n <= 1000, compute dp[i] as the longest valid subsequence ending at index i, with a parent pointer prev[i] to reconstruct the path.

hints.title: Path Reconstruction
hints.text: After computing all dp values, track the index with the maximum length and backtrack through prev pointers.

hints.title: Implementation

complexity.notes: Quadratic dynamic programming with path reconstruction.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy choice does not work because Hamming distance graph has multiple branches.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) auxiliary memory for DP and predecessor tables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Apply LIS dynamic programming with parent pointers for path recovery.
